page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Separate the sine factor from cos x
steps.margin_note: First mark. Only sin(ax)/x is indeterminate; cos x is 1 at x = 0 and is simply substituted. Split them before doing anything else.
lines: At x = 0, sin ax = 0 and x cos x = 0, so the form is 0/0.
Split the expression into the indeterminate part and the ordinary part.
Multiply and divide the first factor by a so the angle ax appears below the sine.

recall.must_convey: That the expression is split into sin(ax)/x and 1/cos x, and that sin(ax)/x is written as a · sin(ax)/(ax).
accept: split it into sin a x over x and one over cos x
multiply and divide by a so the angle a x sits below the sine
cos x is not indeterminate so keep it separate
sin a x by x ni a tho multiply divide cheyyali
take the a outside as a coefficient
heard_as: sin a x by a x

steps.why: Only the sine factor needs the standard limit; cos x is continuous and non-zero at 0, so separating them keeps the working short and shows which rule applies where.
common_mistakes: Cancelling x against the x inside sin ax.
Writing lim sin(ax)/x = 1 and losing the factor a.
steps.memory_tip: sin θ / θ → 1 needs the same angle above and below. Here the angle is ax, so create ax below, and put an a outside so the value is unchanged.

steps.label: Apply lim sin θ / θ = 1
steps.margin_note: Second mark. As x → 0 the angle ax → 0, so the sine bracket is 1, and cos 0 = 1. Only the coefficient a survives.
lines: As x → 0, ax → 0, so lim(x → 0) sin(ax)/(ax) = 1.
Also cos x → cos 0 = 1, so 1/cos x → 1.

recall.must_convey: That sin(ax)/(ax) → 1 and 1/cos x → 1, so the answer is a.
accept: both factors are one so the answer is a
cos zero is one so it does not change the value
sin a x over a x tends to one

steps.why: cos x contributes nothing because cos 0 = 1, so the answer is the coefficient of x inside the sine. The value checks numerically: with a = 3 the expression is 3.0000 at x = 0.0001.
common_mistakes: Answering 1 by ignoring the coefficient a.
Treating cos x as 0 at x = 0 and concluding that the limit does not exist.
steps.memory_tip: Read the answer straight off the question: whatever multiplies x inside the sine is the answer, since cos 0 = 1 leaves it unchanged.

insider_note: Only sin(ax)/x is indeterminate; cos x is simply 1 at x = 0, so separate the two first. Multiply and divide by a so the angle matches below the sine, and that a is the answer.
